title: Paper 1 Model Answer Islam Walkthrough
summary: Paper 1 model answer Islam walkthrough with the current IB World Religions format, timing strategy, stimulus analysis, and a concise worked response plan.
body_markdown:
A strong IB World Religions response is not the one that contains everything you know about Islam. It is the one that selects the right knowledge, connects it directly to the stimulus, and explains its religious significance within the available time.


This **paper 1 model answer Islam** walkthrough covers the current Paper 1 structure, a practical 75-minute plan, and a worked example on zakat. Although older materials describe each question as 3 + 7 marks, the current format uses **3 marks for part (a) and 6 marks for part (b)** . You answer five stimulus questions in 1 hour 15 minutes, producing a maximum of 45 marks.


RevisionDojo's guide to[IB World Religions misconceptions](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-world-religions-misconceptions) can help you identify other assumptions that quietly weaken otherwise knowledgeable answers.


### Paper 1 format at a glance


Before practising your writing, make sure you are preparing for the correct assessment.


- The paper lasts **1 hour 15 minutes** .
- It presents **nine stimulus-response questions** , one for each religion included in Part 1 of the course.
- You answer **five questions** , based on the religions studied by your school.
- Each question has two parts.
- Part (a) is worth **3 marks** .
- Part (b) is worth **6 marks** under the current format.
- Five complete responses produce a maximum of **45 marks** .


Older resources may call these five 10-mark questions divided into 3 + 7 marks. That was the earlier structure. An amendment introduced for examinations from May 2017 reduced part (b) from 7 marks to 6.


Always use the allocation printed on the examination paper. If your teacher uses a legacy 3 + 7 task for extended practice, the same method applies, but the additional mark requires further supported development.


### The 15-minute strategy for each response


Seventy-five minutes divided across five answers gives an average of **15 minutes per religion** . Spending 22 minutes on a polished first response means borrowing seven minutes from an answer you have not yet seen.


A practical allocation is:


- **2 minutes:** read the stimulus, command terms, and both parts
- **4 minutes:** answer the 3-mark question
- **8 minutes:** write the 6-mark explanation
- **1 minute:** check stimulus references and correct obvious errors


Treat these timings as a stopping rule rather than a rigid script. A quick part (a) may leave more time for part (b). At 15 minutes, move on and return later if time remains.


A student tries to push a tower of books through a doorway labelled 15 minutes while another carries only what the question asks


The mistake is common: students try to force an entire topic into a narrow question. Relevance earns more than volume.


### How to read Paper 1 stimulus questions


A stimulus is not decoration. It provides the evidence from which your response should move into accurate religious knowledge.


Read it in three passes:


### Find the visible detail


Underline concrete words, actions, objects, or beliefs. In an Islam question, these might include giving money, purification, intention, prayer, fasting, equality, pilgrimage, revelation, or submission to Allah.


Do not interpret everything immediately. First establish what the source actually says or shows.


### Identify the Islamic concept


Translate each relevant detail into precise subject vocabulary. Giving to eligible recipients may connect to **zakat** . A statement about divine unity may relate to **tawhid** . Washing before prayer may indicate **wudu** , while facing Makkah during salah connects to the **qibla** .


Similar practices are not interchangeable. Zakat is an obligatory pillar for Muslims who meet the relevant conditions, while sadaqah refers more broadly to voluntary charity. Calling every donation zakat removes an important distinction.


### Match the command term


Words such as *identify* , *outline* , and *explain* require different responses. Identification needs accurate recognition. Explanation requires connections: how, why, or with what religious significance?


Use this explanatory chain:


**stimulus detail → Islamic concept → belief or teaching → effect on practice or community**


This prevents your answer from becoming a list of disconnected facts.


### What earns marks in part (a)


Part (a) rewards disciplined observation. Aim for three distinct, relevant points unless the wording requires another structure.


For a stimulus about zakat, three concise points might be:


- The person gives part of their wealth to support people in need.
- The giving is treated as a religious obligation rather than only personal generosity.
- The practice connects worship with responsibility toward the Muslim community.


Each point does a separate job. Repeating that zakat is charitable in different words does not create three ideas. Save wider teaching and consequences for part (b). This protects time and reflects the marks available.


### Building the 6-mark explanation


Part (b) tests more than memory. The examiner needs to see that you understand the concept in relation to both the stimulus and Islam.


A reliable paragraph has four moves:


1. Make a focused claim.
2. Refer to a specific feature of the stimulus.
3. Explain the relevant Islamic belief or practice.
4. Develop its significance for Muslim life.


Two developed paragraphs are generally stronger than six undeveloped statements. Include only knowledge that advances the explanation.


This is why[active recall with IB practice questions](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/active-recall-for-ib-practice-questions) is more useful than repeatedly reading a finished answer. RevisionDojo Study Notes and Flashcards can establish the content, while the Questionbank turns it into timed application. The guide to[retrieval practice for IB revision](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/retrieval-practice-ib-revision) explains how to build this sequence deliberately.


### Short worked Islam example


The following is a teacher-created practice stimulus, not an official examination extract.


**Stimulus:** A Muslim shopkeeper calculates a portion of qualifying wealth and distributes it through a community organization supporting eligible families. The shopkeeper describes the payment as both worship and purification.


**Part (a): Identify three features of zakat shown in the stimulus. \[3\]**


**Model answer:**


The shopkeeper gives a calculated portion of qualifying wealth. The money is distributed to eligible recipients through the community. The payment is understood as an act of worship that purifies wealth and the giver.


This response provides three distinct details and uses accurate terminology without explaining consequences that belong in part (b).


**Part (b): Explain how the stimulus shows the religious significance of zakat in Islam. \[6\]**


**Model answer:**


The stimulus presents zakat as an obligation connected to worship, rather than simply an optional act of kindness. By calculating a portion of qualifying wealth, the shopkeeper recognizes that material possessions carry responsibilities before Allah. The reference to purification reflects the idea that giving can challenge selfish attachment to wealth and encourage obedience.


Zakat also has communal significance because the payment supports eligible families. It connects individual devotion with social responsibility, helping wealth move toward people entitled to assistance. The stimulus therefore shows that worship in Islam can shape both a Muslim's relationship with Allah and the welfare of the wider community.


The answer explains obligation, purification, obedience, and community support while returning to the stimulus. For a legacy 7-mark task, another supported dimension could explain how regular obligatory giving strengthens solidarity within the ummah.


### Common weaknesses and how to fix them


### Retelling the stimulus


Paraphrasing proves that you can read, but not necessarily that you understand the religion. After referring to a detail, ask: **What does this reveal about Islamic belief or Muslim practice?**


### Writing everything about Islam


An answer on zakat does not automatically need paragraphs on salah, sawm, or hajj. Wider links help only when they clarify the role of worship.


### Treating Muslims as identical


Use careful phrasing such as “Muslims may” or “many Muslims.” Islam contains diverse communities, interpretations, cultures, and lived experiences. Do not present one local custom as universal doctrine.


### Memorizing complete essays


Memorized prose is fragile because stimuli change. Memorize flexible units instead: key terms, definitions, belief-practice connections, examples, and paragraph structures.[Spaced repetition for IB revision](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/spaced-repetition-ib-revision-science) can keep those units available over time.


### A focused RevisionDojo practice routine


Start with one concept, such as zakat, tawhid, salah, or revelation. Review it using Study Notes, then close the notes and retrieve definitions and connections through Flashcards. Answer one stimulus question from the Questionbank without support.


Next, use AI Chat to clarify distinctions and the Grading tools to inspect relevance, development, and terminology. Record one actionable correction, then attempt a similar question.[Revision methods used by successful IB students](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-top-ib-students-structure-revision) can turn this into a sustainable weekly routine.


Closer to the examination, combine Predicted Papers and Mock Exams with strict 75-minute timing. The Coursework Library and Tutors can support other parts of World Religions, but Paper 1 fluency comes from writing answers. If long sessions leave little usable knowledge, read the guide to[remembering what you study](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-study-all-day-remember-nothing) or compare[10 proven IB study techniques](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/10-proven-study-techniques-for-ib-students-master-your-revision) .


### The final lesson


Paper 1 rewards selection. The stimulus gives you a narrow doorway, and your task is not to push the whole textbook through it. Choose precise evidence, name the Islamic concept, explain its significance, and stop when the marks have been served.

Knowledge matters. The examination rewards knowledge that arrives in the right place at the right time.
